problems.title: Choose the nearest trigonometric root
problems.question: Among roots of $\cos(2\pi x)/(1+\tan\pi x)=0$, find the one nearest to √13.
problems.idea: Keep the exact domain and use a convenient trigonometric or geometric model.
formulas: The numerator vanishes at $x=1/4+k/2$. The denominator excludes the subfamily x=3/4+n where tanπx=−1. Thus the permitted roots are x=1/4+n.
steps: Since √13≈3.60555, the adjacent permitted roots are 3.25 and 4.25. The midpoint is 3.75, and √13<3.75 because 13<(15/4)². Thus 3.25 is closer than 4.25; all other permitted roots are farther away.

problems.title: A trigonometric system with a radical
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{\sin x}\cos y=0$, $2\sin^2x-\cos^2y-2=0$.
problems.idea: Keep the exact domain and use a convenient trigonometric or geometric model.
formulas: The radical requires sin x≥0. The second equation gives $2\sin^2x=2+\cos^2y$.
steps: The left side is at most 2 and the right side at least 2. Hence sin²x=1 and cos y=0. The radical domain selects sin x=1. These values also make the first equation zero.

problems.title: A rectangle section of a triangular pyramid
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid SABC has base side 12 and lateral edge 15. A plane through the height foot O is parallel to SA and BC. Find the section are a.
problems.idea: Keep the exact domain and use a convenient trigonometric or geometric model.
formulas: O is the base centroid, so its barycentric A-coordinate is 1/3. A plane parallel to SA and BC preserves the sum of its S- and A-coordinates, which is therefore 1/3.
steps: It meets AB, AC at points having A-weight 1/3, and SB, SC at points having S-weight 1/3. Thus the section has one pair of sides parallel to BC of length(2/3)·12=8, and another pair parallel to SA of length 15/3=5.
In a regular triangular pyramid, SA lies in the symmetry plane perpendicular to BC. Thus the section is a rectangle. Its are a is 8·5.

problems.title: Distances from a square pyramid’s base centre
problems.question: The centre O of a regular square pyramid’s base is √14 from a lateral face and 4 from a lateral edge. Find total surface are a divided by base are a.
problems.idea: Keep the exact domain and use a convenient trigonometric or geometric model.
formulas: Write half the base side as b and height as h. The two distances are $bh/\sqrt{h^2+b^2}$ and $\sqrt2bh/\sqrt{h^2+2b^2}$.
steps: Squaring and reciprocating gives 1/b²+1/h²=1/14 and 1/(2b²)+1/h²=1/16. Subtract to get b²=56, and then h²=56/3.
The face apothem is l=√(h²+b²)=2b/√3. Lateral are a is 4bl and base are a 4b². Their ratio is l/b=2/√3. Add 1 for the base.

problems.title: A frustum section determines a dihedral angle
problems.question: In a regular square frustum, the diagonal-section are a equals one lateral-face are a. Find its dihedral angle at the larger base.
problems.idea: Keep the exact domain and use a convenient trigonometric or geometric model.
formulas: For base sides a>b, height h, and face apothem l, the areas are $\sqrt2(a+b)h/2$ and $(a+b)l/2$.
steps: Equality gives l=√2h. Since l²=h²+((a−b)/2)², this forces h=(a−b)/2. The dihedral-angle tangent is h/((a−b)/2)=1.

problems.title: A factored trigonometric equation
problems.question: Solve $\sin5x+\sin x+2\sin^2x=\sqrt3\tan(\arcsin(\sqrt3/2)-\arctan(1/\sqrt3))$.
problems.idea: Keep the exact domain and use a convenient trigonometric or geometric model.
formulas: The inverse angles are π/3 and π/6, so the right side is 1. Use $\sin5x+\sin x=2\sin3x\cos2x$ and $2\sin^2x=1-\cos2x$.
steps: The equation becomes cos 2x(2sin3x−1)=0. Thus cos 2x=0 or sin 3x=1/2. Solve each standard equation.
problems.answer: $x=\pi/4+\pi k/2$, or $x=\pi/18+2\pi k/3$, or $x=5\pi/18+2\pi k/3$, $k\in\mathbb Z$.

problems.title: Solvability of a parameter equation
problems.question: Find all a for which $\cos2x+a\sin x=2a-7$ has a solution.
problems.idea: Keep the exact domain and use a convenient trigonometric or geometric model.
formulas: Put s=sin x∈[−1,1] and use cos 2x=1−2s². Rearrangement gives $a(2-s)=8-2s^2=2(2-s)(2+s)$.
steps: Since 2−s≥1, it can be cancelled. Thus a=4+2s. As s runs through[−1,1], this covers exactly[2,6].
